findings.finding: Both rage-1509 renders succeeded, passed measurement and are served: neural 650 s for 1351 words in 54 blocks, 0.96x predicted, rendered in 12787 s; jaimla 591 s, 0.97x predicted, rendered in 10091 s. Both public manifests return 200 and their docHash ea495558 matches the page.

The neural success is not evidence for the code fix. That process started about 16:13Z and imports engines.py once at startup, so it ran the old 1800 s wall timeout, about 3 h 08 m under the 30% policy and only its last ~24 min after the 19:21 burst. It shows only that no block took 1800 s of wall time between 16:13Z and 19:21Z under the cap that failed twice that morning.

The jaimla success cannot be credited to the code fix, the burst, or both. It ran on the new code inside the burst window with no per-block wall or CPU time recorded. The record argues against crediting the burst: 187 s per block (10091 s / 54) versus 185 s per block for rage-1059 jaimla under the 30% cap (6860 s / 37); its 7.47 s per word is the slowest jaimla figure recorded.
evidence: /root/rage-render/timings.jsonl (31 rows, whole-render wall time only, no per-block fields)
findings.deciding_experiment: Log wall seconds, CPU seconds (utime+stime) and kill reason for each piper call; then render the same doc with the burst off (cpu.max 30000/100000) twice, old wall limit versus run_until_stalled, while the trainer is active. Credit the fix only if the old-code run dies, or the new-code run completes a block whose wall time exceeded the old limit while CPU kept rising.

findings.finding: Kills are mislabelled in the log. The raised TimeoutExpired carries cpu_budget_s as its timeout and holds the kill reason only in exc.reason, which str(exc) omits, so a stall or wall-ceiling kill still logs 'timed out after 1800.0 seconds', the very wording this commit calls misleading.
evidence: python3 -c: TimeoutExpired(['piper'],1800.0) with .reason set prints "Command '['piper']' timed out after 1800.0 seconds"

findings.finding: The CPU accounting has no blind spot for piper as deployed: piper is one python3 process with 3 threads and no children, so /proc/<pid>/stat utime+stime captures its onnxruntime work. The new code is live for the current render (rage-1053 neural started 01:11:55Z, after the deploy).

This record's target cannot be checked by a stranger. The target repository is private, the commit exists only on the AgenticPlace remote, and prod is not publicly readable; the only publicly checkable artifacts are the two rage-1509 manifests and their docHash. Ruling: this is PRIVATE EVIDENCE. The commit id and file md5s fix the state reviewed, but only readers with repository access can verify them; the remedy is labelling, not publishing.
evidence: gh repo view AgenticPlace/mindX --json isPrivate -> true

rationale: The fix is sound: a wall-clock timeout on a throttled process measures contention, not a hang, and the committed runner passes its 7 tests and runs on prod as committed in every line that governs piper. Under the law of verification or unknown, however, rage-1509's recovery is not evidence that the fix works: neural succeeded on the old code, and jaimla ran on the new code at the same seconds per block as a render under the 30% cap, with nothing recorded to show a block would have crossed the old limit. The claimed root cause is likewise unproven, since 26 of 31 renders completed under the same cap. The code is approved; the causal claims remain not yet known, and the conditions are the experiments that would decide them.
conditions: Per-call telemetry: each piper invocation in render_neural/docspeech and render_jaimla appends doc, voice, block, words, wall_s, cpu_s and kill reason; verifiable when the next render of any article adds one row per block.

Honest kill labels: a kill writes exc.reason into the queue log, so a stall kill's line contains 'hung', 'CPU budget' or 'wall ceiling'; verifiable by grepping /var/log/rage-render-queue.log after any kill, or by a unit test asserting the reason appears in the rendered message.

Attribution recorded (requires condition 1): an entry in docs/IMPROVEMENT_JOURNAL.md or the render log states whether at least one block whose wall time exceeded the old limit (1800 s neural, max(900, 20*words) jaimla) completed with CPU still progressing and no burst active, or says 'fix not yet exercised'; verifiable against the telemetry rows.

Stale-marker fix confirmed live: after PID 3160585's pass ends on its own (no restart ordered), the next pass's fd 10 points to a non-deleted /root/render_rage_queue.sh with md5 96217fc7f6d895981916354417b624b2; verifiable with ls -la /proc/<pid>/fd and md5sum.

Manual record edits logged: any hand reset of failure records (such as the *.failed.* -> *.timedout.* rename) is written to /var/log/rage-render-queue.log with a UTC timestamp and reason, and /root/apply_processor_shares.sh (36d92294) is reconciled with scripts/apply_processor_shares.sh (0058dad4); verifiable by grep and md5.
risks_watched: Wall-time headroom: with a per-block wall ceiling of at least 4 h, a chronically starved slice (the live sample ran at 6.1% of a core) no longer fails fast, so a real contention episode can hold the single queue for hours per block, silently, behind newer publishes; watch speak-slice throttled_usec deltas and the per-block wall time from condition 1.
History erased by hand: render-ledger failure history is now editable outside the ledger (the .timedout rename), so a 'store complete' state is only as true as the untouched *.failed.* records.
